books.section: Topic 1.4 Columbian Exchange, Spanish Exploration, and Conquest
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: The Americas had almost no domesticated farm animals to send to Europe.
Native peoples had no experience raising animals before 1492.
options.misconception: Native peoples raised turkeys and dogs; the point is the small number of domesticated species, not none at all.

options.text: Europeans refused to eat meat from animals raised in the Americas.
options.misconception: Europeans did eat turkey; the point is how few farm animals the Americas had.

options.text: The turkey was the most valuable animal traded across the Atlantic.
options.misconception: The table says nothing about value; the turkey's importance is that it was the exception.

rationales.general:
1. Count the animals. Horses, cattle, and pigs went west; only the turkey went east.
2. Ask why the flow was one-sided. The Americas had few domesticated farm animals.
3. Check the claim. Native peoples did raise turkeys and dogs, so the point is few, not none.
4. Rule out the rest. Europeans ate turkey gladly, and the table says nothing about value.
Remember: when a flow runs one way, ask what the sending side had to send.
rationales.A: The Americas had almost no domesticated farm animals, so only the turkey went east while horses, cattle, and pigs went west.
rationales.B: Native peoples raised turkeys and dogs. The point is the small number of domesticated species, not none at all.
rationales.C: Europeans did eat turkey. The point is how few farm animals the Americas had to send.
rationales.D: The table says nothing about value. The turkey matters because it was the one exception.

stem: The table shows that the turkey was the only farm animal to move eastbound. What does this fact best show about the Columbian Exchange?
